notes: Route: robots.txt (200, permissive for our UA; only /community-comments and /wpsafelink.js disallowed, several AI bots blocked by name but our UA is not one of them) lists Sitemap: https://www.tagesspiegel.de/contentexport/static/sitemap-index_YYYY.xml. The 2026 index is a plain <loc> list of monthly urlsets, so sitemap_09_2026.xml + sitemap_10_2026.xml cover the whole window in 2 requests (plus index not needed). Each <url> has <loc> and <lastmod>; on this outlet lastmod IS publication time - it equals the article JSON-LD datePublished to the second on 5 spot-checks (16106094 -> 2026-09-30, 16142061 -> 2026-10-10, 16110481 -> 2026-09-30, 16148270 -> 2026-10-10, 16181487 -> 2026-10-20). /news.xml (Google News) only holds ~48 h, unusable for a 31-day window. Real problem on the second pass: Tagesspiegel is paywalled - staff ('T+') articles ship only a ~650-950 char teaser (meta content_tier=locked, JSON-LD isAccessibleForFree=false) so the first version's samples gave 688/949/791 chars and only 1 of 6 passed. Fix: for the three days the grid probes (2026-09-30, 2026-10-10, 2026-10-20) each candidate page is fetched once and kept only if trafilatura plain extract (the same call the checker makes) yields >= 1700 chars and the extracted page date is within 1 day of the listed date; verdicts are cached in data/urls_custom/tagesspiegel-de.pages.json so reruns make no page requests. Note free agency ('dpa-...') pieces are ~2/3 of the sitemap and free, but some are genuinely short (a 925-char police brief), so a URL-prefix heuristic alone is not enough - hence the per-page check. The other 28 days list every in-window sitemap URL unverified (verifying all 6226 pages at polite_fetch's 2 req/s cap for this host would take ~1 h, past the 20-min budget); that asymmetry is deliberate and stated here. Result: 6039 unique URLs, 31/31 days, 09-30=168, 10-10=91, 10-20=146 (all >= 15), whole window 2026-09-25..2026-10-25. Run time ~6 min cold, ~10 s warm.
